description: Generalize char(c) into atomic parsers for predicates, anchored regular expressions, literal strings, and end-of-input.

steps.description: Alongside char(c), define satisfy(pred, name), which tests s[pos] against a predicate function pred and advances to pos + 1 on success.
Define regex(pattern, flags), which compiles pattern once and calls rx.match(s, pos) to match anchored at pos, returning (m.group(0), m.end()).
Define lit(string) to check the slice s[pos:pos+n] == string, and eof() to succeed with (None, pos) only when pos == len(s).

steps.answer: whitespace matches the two leading spaces and returns ('  ', 2), and lit('if') matches the slice s[0:2] and returns ('if', 2).
steps.question: What do whitespace('  abc', 0) and lit('if')('if x', 0) return?

steps.description: Build digit, alpha, and whitespace from satisfy and regex, then test them along with lit('if').
Watch regex(r'\s+') match the two spaces at the start of '  abc' and return ('  ', 2).

title: Atomic Parsers: satisfy, regex, lit, and eof
